cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Outsmart the Room
cards.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Don't open the delivery email. Let me deduce where our office biscuits went. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for them. I'll tell everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Wait. That's a clue, not a conclusion. I should announce the solution.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Too late. They're downstairs opening the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them nobody eats until I identify the contents. Finding a box doesn't mean they've solved the biscuits.

mechanism: A directs finding office biscuits but turns B location clue and others opening the box into a race to control the final announcement, offering plates to retain cooperation.
confusable: Unlike only claiming credit for a past discovery, A keeps redefining what must be solved or announced first as others progress; authority accommodates their actions while reserving the win.
comparison: A group already retrieving snacks differs from two puzzle solvers whose simultaneous answer forces a new priority rule.
seedUse: D139-a delivery email, reception and box opening; S02-a changes the group task after B beats A to the obvious conclusion.
